whatIsVeganism.title: What is veganism?
whatIsVeganism.description: “Veganism is a way of living which seeks to exclude, as far as is possible and practicable all forms of exploitation of, and cruelty to, animals for food, clothing or any other purpose.”
whatIsVeganism.definition: A compassionate way of living that touches food, clothing, and beyond.

whyGoVegan.title: Why go vegan?
whyGoVegan.subtitle: Five powerful reasons to choose compassion over cruelty.

animals.title: For the Animals
animals.content: More than 80 billion land animals are slaughtered for food every year. By weight, farmed animals now make up about 70% of all birds and 60% of all mammals on Earth. Most spend their short lives on crowded industrial farms.
animals.full:
More than 80 billion land animals are slaughtered for food every year. That figure doesn't include fish, which are counted by the tonne rather than individually: an estimated 1–2 trillion wild fish are caught each year.

By weight, farmed poultry now make up about 70% of all birds on Earth, and livestock about 60% of all mammals. Humans account for 36%, and wild mammals just 4%.

Most of these animals are intelligent, sensitive beings raised in crowded industrial systems and slaughtered very young. Chickens bred for meat, for example, are typically slaughtered at around 5–7 weeks old.

As more people learn how animals are raised and killed, many are choosing kinder, plant-based alternatives.

planet.title: For Our Planet
planet.content: Livestock produces about 14.5% of human-caused greenhouse gas emissions — roughly as much as all the world's transport. Animal farming also uses most of the world's farmland and almost a third of agriculture's water footprint.
planet.full:
Livestock supply chains produce about 14.5% of all human-caused greenhouse gas emissions — roughly on a par with the entire transport sector (around 14%).

Animal products account for 29% of the water footprint of global agriculture. Meat, dairy, eggs and fish farming use about 83% of the world's farmland, yet provide just 18% of our calories and 37% of our protein.

Food production is the main driver of biodiversity loss worldwide, and shifting towards plant-based diets is one of the most effective ways to protect nature.

The largest analysis of farms and food products to date, led by researchers at the University of Oxford, found that avoiding animal products is one of the most effective ways an individual can reduce their environmental impact.

health.title: For Personal Health
health.content: Leading dietetic associations agree that well-planned vegan diets are healthy at every stage of life. Studies link plant-based diets to lower cholesterol and a lower risk of type 2 diabetes.
health.full:
Heart disease is the world's leading cause of death, and diabetes is also among the top ten.

The Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics and the British Dietetic Association both state that well-planned vegetarian and vegan diets are healthy and suitable for all stages of life.

A meta-analysis of clinical trials and observational studies found that plant-based diets are associated with lower total and LDL ("bad") cholesterol. In a study of over 60,000 people, vegans had the lowest rate of type 2 diabetes.

As with any diet, planning matters: vegans should get vitamin B12 from fortified foods or a supplement.

publicHealth.title: For Public Health
publicHealth.content: Most new infectious diseases in humans come from animals, and intensive farming is one of the drivers. Around 73% of the world's antimicrobials are used in farmed animals, fuelling drug resistance.
publicHealth.full:
About 60–75% of emerging infectious diseases in humans are zoonotic, meaning they come from animals. The UN Environment Programme lists rising demand for animal protein and unsustainable intensification of farming among the main drivers of new zoonotic diseases such as avian influenza.

Unsafe food makes an estimated 600 million people ill every year. Campylobacter, one of the most common causes of food poisoning, is mainly linked to poultry, raw milk and undercooked meat.

Around 73% of all antimicrobials sold worldwide are used in animals raised for food, partly to promote growth or prevent disease in crowded conditions. This overuse speeds up antimicrobial resistance, making infections in people harder to treat.

humanRights.title: For People
humanRights.content: Around 670 million people faced hunger in 2024, yet more than a third of the world's crop calories are fed to animals. Growing food for people instead could feed billions more.
humanRights.full:
An estimated 638–720 million people faced hunger in 2024.

Meanwhile, 36% of the calories produced by the world's crops are used as animal feed, and only about 12% of those calories end up in the human diet as meat, dairy and eggs. Animal farming uses around 83% of the world's farmland, yet provides only 18% of our calories.

One study estimated that growing crops for people to eat directly, rather than for animal feed and biofuels, could feed around 4 billion more people.

Hunger has many causes, including conflict, poverty and inequality, but using land and crops more efficiently would make it easier to feed everyone.

kindnessCallout.lineOne: Kinder to animals, kinder to our planet, kinder to humans.

faqs.title: Vegan FAQs
faqs.subtitle: Common questions about the vegan lifestyle.

difficult.question: Is it difficult to live vegan?
difficult.answer: No. It can take a little time to figure out in the beginning, but following a vegan lifestyle has never been easier. These days there is an abundance of vegan-friendly products readily available.

eat.question: What do vegans eat?
eat.answer: Vegans eat the same basic things as everyone else: vegetables, fruit, rice, grains, tofu, beans, along with plant-based versions of burgers, hot dogs, pizza, ramen, and more.

nutrition.question: Can I meet all my nutritional requirements?
nutrition.answer: Yes! The Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics and the British Dietetic Association both say that well-planned vegan diets are suitable for people of all ages. The most important nutrient to plan for is vitamin B12 — get it from fortified foods or a supplement.

religion.question: Is veganism a religion or a cult?
religion.answer: Absolutely not. While some vegans follow religions, others don’t.

unsure.question: I’m interested, but unsure. What should I do?
unsure.answer: We suggest increasing the amount of vegan meals you eat, while continuing to educate yourself. Join our events or online vegan groups to find friends and ask questions.
